features.title: Data directory
features.behavior: kb init creates the data directory, seeds the sample documents, records metadata, and writes its first log event.

features.title: Document list
features.behavior: kb list reports every known document with id, title, filename, line count, and origin, from the metadata index alone.

features.title: Document import
features.behavior: kb import copies a new file into the data directory, records it with metadata, and logs what it did.

features.title: Document detail
features.behavior: kb show returns the imported document's metadata entry plus its full content.

evidence.observed:
exit 0: {"id":"field-guide","title":"Field guide to importing","filename":"field-guide.md","lines":20,"origin":"imported","metadata":{"chars":841,"words":142,"paragraphs":6},"content":"# Field guide to importing

Importing is the moment a document becomes part of the knowledge base
instead of a file that happens to sit nearby. The import command copies
the file into the documents folder and, just as important, records it in
the metadata index.

## Why the metadata index exists

A directory scan tells you what files exist; the metadata index tells you
what the system knows. Listing reads the index, never the directory, so
the answer to "what is in the knowledge base" comes from recorded state
rather than rediscovery. That is the system of record principle applied
to a single JSON file.

## What survives a restart

Everything: the copied document, its index entry, its title and line
count. A fresh process lists the imported document without re-reading the
original source, which is the whole point of persistence.
"}

features.title: Metadata extraction
features.behavior: Every recorded entry carries chars, words, and paragraph counts extracted from its content.

evidence.observed:
exit 0: {"id":"architecture-notes","title":"Architecture notes","filename":"architecture-notes.md","lines":25,"origin":"seeded","metadata":{"chars":1017,"words":175,"paragraphs":8},"content":"# Architecture notes

The kb tool is one program with two faces: a command line interface for
scripted use and a small local HTTP server for interactive use. Both faces
call the same functions, so behavior never depends on the invoking face.

## Storage

All state lives in a data directory that the init command creates. Inside
it, a documents folder holds the imported text and markdown files, and an
index folder is reserved for derived structures. Nothing is stored outside
the data directory, and deleting it returns the tool to a clean state.

## Answering

Answers carry citations that name the source document and the exact line
they quote. An answer without a citation is treated as a bug, not a
feature. The composer that turns citations into prose is deliberately
simple; it marks the seam where a language model would sit in a real
assistant.

## Boundaries

The HTTP server binds to the loopback interface only and talks to the same
storage layer as the command line. No network calls leave the machine.
"}

features.title: Metadata persistence
features.behavior: A fresh process lists the imported document from index/documents-meta.json alone.

features.title: Document chunking
features.behavior: kb index chunks every known document deterministically into index/chunks.json with per-document sha256.

features.title: Index status
features.behavior: kb status reports documents, indexed count, total chunks, state (including corrupt), and the offending documents, from disk only.

features.title: Question answering
features.behavior: kb ask answers with at most two chunk citations from the ready index, refuses otherwise, and logs both outcomes.
features.verification: kb ask --data-dir kb-data "Which lines become citations in the ranking?"

features.title: App starts
features.behavior: kb serve --self-check binds the loopback HTTP server, answers /health, /documents, the first detail, and /status, and shuts down cleanly.

features.title: Structured logging
features.behavior: Mutating commands and ask append sequence-numbered events to log/events.jsonl; kb logs filters them by level and event.

features.title: Corruption recovery
features.behavior: kb index --rebuild re-chunks every document regardless of the sha gate, the recovery for empty-chunk corruption.

features.title: Architecture guard
features.behavior: kb guard executes the layer rules as behavior: read-only server, storage containment, disposable derived state.

features.title: Document delete
features.behavior: kb delete removes the document file, the index entry, and the chunk record, and logs it; kb index reconciles any orphan a half-done delete leaves.

features.title: Verified-work ladder
features.behavior: kb ladder replays the scripted work item under three role configurations and exits 0 only when the rubric scores strictly climb.
